meta.title: Interactive Sales Analytics Dashboard | Sāra 0004 | TriSaar Consulting
meta.description: Sāra 0004 case study: a self-contained browser-native sales analytics dashboard that reads Excel data locally, provides interactive KPI and chart views, and enables filtering across regions, products, and channels.

data.text: Transforming static spreadsheet reporting into an interactive, filterable dashboard for faster business insight.
A self-contained HTML dashboard that reads Excel data in-browser, renders KPI cards, trends and category views, and lets users explore performance across regions, products and channels.

data.title: From static spreadsheets to a live, interactive analytics experience.
data.subtitle: We transformed a recurring spreadsheet reporting process into a self-contained dashboard that loads Excel data directly in the browser and makes common performance questions easier to answer.

pillars.label: Challenge
pillars.title: Reporting was trapped in static spreadsheets.
pillars.body: Sales teams relied on manually updated Excel workbooks with limited ways to explore performance across regions, products and channels.

points.text: Weekly reporting cycles left data days behind the current period
New questions often required manual pivots or report changes
Regional managers depended on the analytics team for tailored views

pillars.label: Solution
pillars.title: A browser-native dashboard that reads Excel locally.
pillars.body: We engineered a self-contained HTML dashboard using SheetJS for in-browser Excel parsing and Chart.js for interactive visualization.

steps.text: Load Excel data directly in the browser with SheetJS
Render trends, KPI cards & comparisons with Chart.js
Filter performance by region, product and channel
Generate dynamic pivot views for detailed analysis

pillars.label: Impact
pillars.title: Faster refreshes. Easier exploration. Self-service analysis.
pillars.body: Users can load an updated workbook and explore the resulting analytics without rebuilding a report or waiting for a new custom view.

data.title: Reporting trapped in static spreadsheets.
data.body: Sales teams worked with manually updated Excel reports that were useful for recurring reporting but cumbersome when leaders wanted to explore performance by region, product or channel.

core.label: The Core Challenge
core.body: The data existed, but answering a new business question often meant reworking the report rather than exploring the information directly.

points.title: Stale reporting cycles
points.body: Weekly reporting meant users could be working from data that was several days behind the current period.

points.title: Limited exploration
points.body: Changing the view by region, product or channel often required manual pivoting or a revised report.

points.title: Dependence on analysts
points.body: Regional managers could not always answer their own follow-up questions without requesting a tailored analysis.

points.title: Recurring manual overhead
points.body: Teams spent time rebuilding familiar reporting views instead of using that time for deeper analysis.

impact.label: The Business Impact
impact.body: The reporting process slowed access to insight, created repetitive manual work and made ad-hoc exploration harder than it needed to be.

data.title: A browser-native analytics dashboard built around the existing Excel workflow.
data.intro: We kept Excel as the familiar data source while moving the reporting experience into a self-contained HTML dashboard. Data is parsed locally in the browser, transformed into reusable analytical views and refreshed through interactive controls.

hub.label: Our Approach
hub.body: Separate the data source from the reporting experience: keep the client's familiar Excel input while creating a more flexible way to explore and communicate the data.

steps.title: Design the information hierarchy
steps.body: Structured the dashboard around the questions leaders commonly ask, with KPI cards for headline performance, trend views for movement over time and category views for comparisons.

steps.title: Read Excel data in-browser
steps.body: Used SheetJS to parse compatible .xlsx files client-side, keeping the data-loading workflow lightweight and avoiding a backend data pipeline.
points: No data upload to a server

steps.title: Build interactive visualizations
steps.body: Used Chart.js to turn the workbook data into KPI cards, line charts and bar charts that update as users explore the data.

steps.title: Add live filters and pivot views
steps.body: Added region, product and channel filters that update the dashboard views together, plus a dynamic pivot table for detailed breakdowns.

items.title: Faster refresh
items.body: Updated Excel data can be loaded into the dashboard without rebuilding the reporting views.

items.title: Self-service exploration
items.body: Users can change common dimensions themselves instead of requesting a new report.

items.title: One analytical view
items.body: KPIs, trends, comparisons and detailed pivot views work together in one browser experience.

enablers.label: Key Enablers
enablers.intro: Lightweight browser technologies keep the solution portable and easy to deploy.

data.title: Faster access to insight. Less reporting friction.
data.intro: The dashboard changes the reporting experience from a recurring static deliverable into an interactive analytical surface that users can explore themselves.
